challenge_to_conversation_first_ui.expansion: The ChatGPT surface assumes one addressee, one live turn, and a history whose last entry is the state. Long-running autonomous agents violate all three: the last message about agent-7 may be hours stale while agent-7 has changed mode twice. The user is then asked to hold mode and ownership in memory, which is the classic mode-error precondition; and to reconstruct current state by scrolling, which is a retrieval act that interrupted mobile users skip. This is not an argument for abandoning conversation-first; it is an argument that conversation must be paired with an always-on state surface (P2) and an addressing/readback grammar (P5), otherwise the conversation-first choice quietly transfers the state-holding burden from the software to the human.

challenge_to_conversation_first_ui.one_line: Transcript position is not run state: a ChatGPT-style thread linearises concurrent, long-lived, mutable runs into an append-only history, so at fleet scale the mode, the owner, and the current state of any given agent become memory-resident rather than surface-resident.
challenge_to_conversation_first_ui.sharpest_form: If a user cannot answer 'is agent X in dry-run or live, and who owns it' without scrolling, conversation-first has failed regardless of how good the messages are.

prediction.headline_answer: QUALIFIED_YES_WITH_THREE_HARD_AMENDMENTS. Conversation-first is defensible on mobile only if (a) a glanceable status strip lives permanently outside the top menu, (b) conversation carries a three-grain consent vocabulary plus a since-last-seen handover digest rather than a running narration, and (c) every approval carries a faithful trace excerpt so that reserving raw xterm for desktop removes the authoring surface but never the evidence surface. Unamended, the proposal fails at fleet scale and after surprise.

paths.claim: Universe mobile should keep the ChatGPT-style thread as the primary input affordance, but its payload should be restricted to three grains of consent (silent-and-logged, notify-and-proceed, hard-blocking ask) plus a since-last-seen handover digest. Progress narration is demoted to the status surface.
paths.falsifier: If cold-open users reconstruct fleet state at least as accurately from raw scrollback as from a digest, the digest is unnecessary and pure conversation-first survives unamended.
predicted_design_moves: Three-grain consent picker set per fleet/agent at delegation time, readable on the surface, changeable only with an explicit confirmation.
A single 'what changed while you were away' digest generated on cold app open, ordered by state-change, not by timestamp of chatter.
Blocking asks are the only messages permitted to interrupt; notify-and-proceed lands in an inbox; silent lands only in the trace.
paths.title: Conversation as consent-and-handover channel, not as the state surface
paths.why: Derived-field convergence across all three packs (reattach/handover, consent grain, faithful trace) is the strongest signal available and it points at delegation envelopes, not at chat completeness. Per-action narration in a thread converts a delegation envelope into a per-action approval regime, which the social-delegation seeds say is the failure mode of standing delegation.

paths.claim: Putting Goal/Fleet/Galaxy/Rooms behind a top menu is fine. Putting status behind that same menu is the one placement that should be rejected. A fixed, small, glance-readable status vocabulary must remain on the primary surface at all times.
paths.falsifier: If interrupted users answer 'which agents are blocked right now' within a low latency threshold from a menu-only build, the persistent strip is redundant.
predicted_design_moves: A persistent one-line strip: N running / N waiting-on-you / N failed, with a hard cap on distinct status tokens.
Mode (autonomous vs supervised, dry-run vs live) rendered as a persistent badge, never as a past chat message.
The strip is the only always-on element; everything else may live behind the menu.
paths.title: Status must not go behind the top menu; the menu holds depth, not state
paths.why: Glanceable-status and cockpit-mode seeds in all three packs converge on the same requirement: the mode and the health must be readable from the surface, not recalled from memory or retrieved by navigation. A menu makes state a retrieval act, and retrieval acts are skipped under interruption.

paths.claim: Reserving raw xterm for desktop is correct as an authoring and scrubbing decision and wrong if it is read as an evidence decision. Each mobile blocking ask should carry a bounded, verbatim, non-summarised trace excerpt (the exact command/diff/output that motivated the ask) with one gesture to the full trace.
paths.falsifier: If detection of an injected wrong-summary is statistically equal with and without the verbatim excerpt, the excerpt is decoration and summary-only approval is acceptable.
predicted_design_moves: Excerpt is quoted, byte-faithful, and visibly marked as verbatim vs model-authored.
'Open full trace' is available on mobile read-only; authoring/interactive shell is desktop-only.
Approvals cannot be granted from a surface that shows only a summary.
paths.stance_on_question: supports the xterm split, amends its consequence
paths.title: Raw xterm to desktop, but a faithful trace excerpt must ride with every mobile approval
paths.why: The trust seeds distinguish a faithful trace from a persuasive narrative and say the difference matters most after a surprise. A mobile approval built on a model-authored summary is precisely the persuasive-narrative case, and it is the case where consent is least informed.

paths.claim: 'Surface only approvals/blockers in conversation' is the right instinct but underspecified: approvals, blockers, retries, and progress are four different channels. If they share one thread, N concurrent agents produce the software equivalent of alarm flood and the real blocker is missed.
paths.falsifier: If miss-rate on a planted blocker does not degrade as concurrent agent count rises in a single-thread build, channel separation is premature optimisation.
predicted_design_moves: Retries and self-recovered errors never enter the conversation; they enter the trace and, at most, increment a counter on the status strip.
Explicit acknowledgement state per blocker, with escalation if unacknowledged past a threshold.
Per-fleet muting that mutes progress but is structurally incapable of muting a hard-blocking ask.
paths.stance_on_question: adds a precondition the proposal omits
paths.title: Alarm channel and status channel must be separated before fleet scale, not after
paths.why: Control-room and dashboard seeds in all three packs independently insist that demand-for-action and status must not share a channel, and that acknowledgement/escalation is a separate act from reading.

paths.claim: Conversation-first is a single-addressee grammar. With a fleet, every message needs an explicit owner, an explicit addressee, and a readback confirmation on ownership transfer. Predicted position: conversation-first holds up to a small number of concurrently-active agents and should degrade to a Rooms/place model above it, rather than scaling the thread.
paths.falsifier: If users maintain correct ownership attribution in a flat thread at high concurrency, the room degradation is unnecessary.
predicted_design_moves: Every agent utterance carries an unambiguous agent identity token in the same fixed vocabulary as the status strip.
Ownership transfer requires a readback confirmation, not a silent reassignment.
A measured threshold at which the default surface switches from thread to room list.
paths.title: At multi-agent scale the thread needs addressing, ownership, and readback, or it should yield to Rooms
paths.why: Multi-agent seeds across all three packs independently name explicit ownership, explicit handoff, and confirmation-by-readback as the substrate, and architecture seeds treat 'places' as determining who sees state and who may speak. A flat transcript supplies none of these.

paths.claim: A linear thread is the natural fit for serial-channel and interrupt-recovery users, which is an argument in favour of conversation-first that the proposal never makes. But its value is conditional on an explicit, addressable 'what changed since I last listened' query, because background agents generate exactly the asynchronous change events a serial channel loses.
paths.falsifier: If screen-reader users recover fleet state from linear scrollback without a delta query at parity accuracy, the delta query is optional.
predicted_design_moves: The handover digest from P1 is exposed as a first-class, announceable, keyboard/voice-addressable query, not only as a visual card.
Every element of the status strip has a non-visual equivalent; no state exists only as a visual card.
Interruption cost budgeted: announcements are capped per unit time.
paths.stance_on_question: supports conversation-first for a reason the proposal does not state
paths.title: Conversation-first is the accessibility-strong choice, but only with an explicit change-since-last-listen query
paths.why: Accessibility seeds in all three packs converge on linearization plus announced events plus recoverable navigation; the missing piece is always the delta query, not the linearity.

structured_result.summary: CLAUDE post-meeting prediction for the Universe mobile conductor question: a conditional yes to conversation-first, but only if the conversation is treated as a consent-and-handover channel rather than the state surface. Five predicted paths (P1-P5) are kept on separate, non-flattened lineage threads back to Meeting Room claims and to frozen pack seed IDs across all three packs. One challenge to conversation-first (transcript position is not run state; mode and ownership become memory-resident at fleet scale), risks, per-path and overall confidence (MEDIUM, with the schema/self-attestation LOW-to-MEDIUM mismatch preserved as unresolved), unresolved dissent (D8, amended D1, X1-X13 unadopted), and seven smallest discriminating prototypes/user tests. Five post-share-only ideas are explicitly flagged. No RAG, Feature Nodes, Goals, or Todos adopted; frozen packs untouched; no web verification performed.
